Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Diagnosis:
1. The failing test `testCalendarTimezoneRespected()` checks that formatting a Calendar in a given timezone produces a string that matches SimpleDateFormat's output in the same timezone.
2. The test sets a non-default timezone on the Calendar and SimpleDateFormat, then compares the formatted results. The failure summary says FastDateFormat's "z" pattern does not respect the timezone of Calendar instances.
3. The FastDateFormat.format(Calendar) method delegates to FastDatePrinter.format(Calendar).
4. FastDatePrinter.format(Calendar) calls `format(calendar, new StringBuffer(...))`.
5. This calls applyRules(Calendar, StringBuffer), which calls each Rule's appendTo method with the Calendar.
6. The timezone formatting is done by a Rule subclass, TimeZoneNameRule.
7. The TimeZoneNameRule.appendTo() implementation appends the timezone display name of the stored zone field, selected via DST offset from the passed Calendar.
8. Crucially, it never queries the Calendar's timezone but only uses its DST offset to decide daylight/standard and always formats the initial TimeZone passed when the Rule was created.
9. Therefore, the "z" pattern in FastDateFormat always formats the timezone used to create the formatter, ignoring the timezone of the actual Calendar passed to the format method.
10. This explains why the time component shows the Calendar's timezone but the "z" pattern suffix always shows the formatter's timezone instead of the Calendar's timezone.
11. The root cause is that TimeZoneNameRule does not use the timezone from the passed Calendar instance but only uses its own timezone field set at construction, violating the contract that formatting a Calendar should respect its timezone.

The failure reproduction and code inspection clearly show that the bug is in FastDatePrinter.TimeZoneNameRule.appendTo, where the timezone used for formatting is taken from the object's stored timezone field, not the Calendar's timezone.

This mismatch causes the pattern "z" to ignore the Calendar's timezone.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
